title: Environment, volumes and profiles
summary: Variable substitution and .env files, env_file, named volumes, and optional services with profiles.

steps.title: Two different .env ideas
body: Compose has two features that both involve "env files" and are easy to confuse:
**1. Interpolation** — `${VAR}` in `compose.yaml` is replaced by Compose *before anything runs*, from your shell's environment or a file named **`.env`** next to the compose file:
image: postgres:${PG_VERSION:-17}          # 17 unless PG_VERSION is set
POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:?set DB_PASSWORD in .env}   # error if missing
- ./api.env          # each KEY=value line becomes a container env var
So `.env` configures **the compose file**; `env_file` configures **the container**. Keep `.env` out of git when it holds secrets, and commit a `.env.example` instead.

steps.prompt: `.env` contains `API_KEY=abc`. The compose file never mentions `API_KEY`. Does the api container see `API_KEY`?
options: No: `.env` only feeds `${...}` interpolation in the compose file
Yes: every container gets all variables from `.env`
steps.explain: To pass it in, write `environment: API_KEY: ${API_KEY}`, or put it in a file referenced by `env_file:`.

steps.prompt: Match each interpolation form to its behaviour.
pairs: the value of TAG, or empty (with a warning) if unset
TAG if set and non-empty, otherwise `dev`
fails with the message if TAG is unset or empty
a literal `$HOME`, passed on to the container's shell

steps.prompt: `.env` contains `PG_VERSION=16`. What image does Compose use for this service?
steps.explain: The default after `:-` only applies when the variable is unset or empty. Run `docker compose config` to see the fully interpolated file.

steps.title: Named volumes and profiles
body: Named volumes are declared at the top level and referenced by services; Compose creates them as `<project>_<name>`:
**Profiles** make services optional. A service with `profiles:` starts only when one of its profiles is enabled (or when you name it explicitly):
docker compose up -d                     services without profiles only
docker compose --profile tools up -d     ... plus adminer

steps.prompt: With the file above plus `db` and `api` (no profiles), which services start on `docker compose --profile tools up -d`?
steps.explain: Services without profiles always start; profiled ones only when a matching profile is enabled.

steps.prompt: Declare and use a named volume for Redis data.
steps.explain: `./redisdata` would be a bind mount of a host folder; `redisdata` refers to the volume declared at the bottom.

steps.title: Interpolate like Compose
prompt: Write `string Interpolate(string text, Dictionary<string, string> vars)` that expands:
- `${NAME:-default}` → the value if present and non-empty, otherwise `default`
- `${NAME:?message}` → the value if present and non-empty; otherwise the **whole result** is `error: message`
starter: string Interpolate(string text, Dictionary<string, string> vars)
solution: string Interpolate(string text, Dictionary<string, string> vars)
if (text[i] == '$' && i + 1 < text.Length && text[i + 1] == '$') { sb.Append('$'); i += 2; continue; }
string name = dash >= 0 ? expr[..dash] : q >= 0 ? expr[..q] : expr;
bool has = vars.TryGetValue(name, out string? value) && value != "";
template: Dojo.Eq("missing plain is empty", "redis:", Interpolate("redis:${REDIS_TAG}", dojoVars));
Dojo.Eq("required missing", "error: set DB_PASSWORD in .env", Interpolate("Password=${DB_PASSWORD:?set DB_PASSWORD in .env}", dojoVars));
Dojo.Eq("escaped dollar and two vars", "echo $HOME app/16", Interpolate("echo $$HOME ${USER}/${PG_VERSION}", dojoVars));
hints: Walk the string with an index; handle `$$` before `${`.
Find the matching `}` with `IndexOf('}', i)` and work on the expression between.
Check for `:-` and `:?` to split the name from the default or message.

steps.title: Which services start?
prompt: Write `List<string> Active(Dictionary<string, List<string>> profiles, List<string> enabled, List<string> named)`.
- `profiles[s]` lists service s's profiles (empty when it has none).
- `named` are services named on the command line (`docker compose up adminer`), which start regardless of profiles.
Return the services that start, sorted alphabetically (ordinal).
starter: List<string> Active(Dictionary<string, List<string>> profiles, List<string> enabled, List<string> named)
solution: List<string> Active(Dictionary<string, List<string>> profiles, List<string> enabled, List<string> named)
template: var dojoProfiles = new Dictionary<string, List<string>> { ["db"] = new(), ["api"] = new(), ["adminer"] = new() { "tools" }, ["k6"] = new() { "perf" }, ["mailpit"] = new() { "tools", "dev" } };
Dojo.Eq("no profiles enabled", new List<string> { "api", "db" }, Active(dojoProfiles, new List<string>(), new List<string>()));
Dojo.Eq("--profile tools", new List<string> { "adminer", "api", "db", "mailpit" }, Active(dojoProfiles, new List<string> { "tools" }, new List<string>()));
Dojo.Eq("--profile dev --profile perf", new List<string> { "api", "db", "k6", "mailpit" }, Active(dojoProfiles, new List<string> { "dev", "perf" }, new List<string>()));
Dojo.Eq("named service", new List<string> { "api", "db", "k6" }, Active(dojoProfiles, new List<string>(), new List<string> { "k6" }));
